title: Shopping & money
goal: Ask prices, point to 'this one' and 'that one', ask for other sizes and colours, bargain politely and pay.
intro:
From the vegetable vendor to the sari shops of Pune's Laxmi Road, shopping in Maharashtra still involves conversation — and often some friendly bargaining (घासाघीस).

The key grammar is the **demonstratives**: हा / ही / हे 'this' and तो / ती / ते 'that', which agree in gender like everything else, and which turn into **या** / **त्या** before a postposition.

vocab.note: f एवढी, n एवढं. 'That much': तेवढा. एवढंच 'only this much'.
m · pl रुपये; oblique pl रुपयां-
Often just घेणे: मी हा घेतो 'I'll take this'.
m · addressed as काका / दादा / शेठ
m · in shops usually साईझ: मोठा साईझ

vocab.en: to take; to buy; to have (food)

phrases.en: Bring it down a bit, please.
Do you have this in a bigger size?

grammar.title: This and that: हा / तो
grammar.body:
Demonstratives agree with the noun:

**this:** हा (m) · ही (f; n pl) · हे (n; m pl) · ह्या (f pl)
**that:** तो (m) · ती (f; n pl) · ते (n; m pl) · त्या (f pl)

Before a postposition they become **या** ('this') and **त्या** ('that'): या दुकानात 'in this shop', त्या साडीची किंमत 'that sari's price', याचा 'of this one'.

'This one / that one' is just the demonstrative alone: **हा** नको, **तो** दाखवा 'not this one, show me that one'. 'Which of these?' = **यातला कोणता?**

examples.en: Not this one — show me that one.
Everything is cheap in that shop.

grammar.title: Prices: कितीला? and 'for … rupees'
grammar.body:
Ask the price with **कितीला?** ('for how much?') or **किती रुपयांचा / ची / चं?** ('of how many rupees?', agreeing with the item). For a total: **किती झाले?**

Give or understand a price with **-ला / -ना** ('for'): शंभर रुपयांना 'for a hundred rupees', दोनशेला 'for two hundred'. Rates are just price + unit: साठ रुपये किलो '60 rupees a kilo'; and दहाला एक 'one for ten'.

Remember the fraction words: **दीडशे** 150, **अडीचशे** 250, **साडेतीनशे** 350, **सव्वाशे** 125.

examples.en: How much are tomatoes a kilo? (market phrase)
This shirt costs five hundred rupees.
How much is it all together?

dialogue.title: Buying a Paithani
dialogue.setting: Smita is shopping for a Paithani silk sari on Laxmi Road, Pune.

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.en: Come in, madam — what can I show you?

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: ही बघा, अगदी नवीन डिझाइन आहे.
lines.roman: hī baghā, agdī navīn ḍizāin āhe.
lines.en: Look at this one — a brand new design.

lines.speaker: Smita
lines.en: It's lovely. How much is it?

lines.speaker: Smita
lines.native: बापरे, खूप महाग आहे! जरा कमी करा ना.
lines.roman: bāpre, khūp mahāg āhe! dzarā kamī karā nā.
lines.en: Goodness, that's very expensive! Bring it down a bit.

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: ताई, ही शुद्ध रेशमाची आहे. अकरा हजार द्या.
lines.roman: tāī, hī shuddha reshmāchī āhe. akrā hadzār dyā.
lines.en: Madam, it's pure silk. Give me eleven thousand.

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.en: All right, take it. For you.

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: हो, चालेल. हा कोड स्कॅन करा.
lines.roman: ho, tsālel. hā koḍ skæn karā.

culture: Bargaining is normal at street stalls, markets and many small clothes shops, but not in supermarkets, malls, chemists or fixed-price ('fixed rate') stores. Keep it good-humoured; a smile and 'जरा कमी करा ना, काका' goes a long way. Mobile UPI payments are everywhere — even the vegetable vendor has a QR code. The **पैठणी** sari from Paithan, with its peacock-patterned border, is Maharashtra's most prized textile.

tip.title: हा, ही, हे — this; तो, ती, ते — that
tip.body:
- 'This' agrees with the noun: **हा** शर्ट (m), **ही** साडी (f), **हे** बूट (m pl) / हे पुस्तक (n).
- 'That' works the same way: **तो**, **ती**, **ते**.
- Before an ending they become **या** / **त्या**: या दुकानात, त्या साडीची किंमत.
- Alone they mean 'this one / that one': हा नको, तो दाखवा.
tip.pattern: हा / ही / हे + noun · या / त्या + noun-ending

sentences.en: Not this one, show me another one.
The colour of these trousers is nice.

tip.title: कितीला? — for how much?
tip.body:
- Ask the price with **कितीला?** or **किती रुपयांचा / ची / चं?**, agreeing with the item: शर्ट … रुपयांचा, साडी … रुपयांची.
- 'For 200 rupees' = दोनशे **रुपयांना**; a rate is just price + unit: साठ रुपये किलो.
- For the total: **किती झाले?**

sentences.en: These trousers are eight hundred rupees.

sentences.native: मी ही साडी दोन हजार रुपयांना घेतली.
sentences.roman: mī hī sāḍī don hadzār rupayānnā ghetlī.
sentences.en: I bought this sari for two thousand rupees.
Tomatoes are sixty rupees a kilo.
I don't have much money on me.
Six mangoes for a hundred rupees.

sentences.native: इथे सगळं महाग आहे, बाजारात स्वस्त आहे.
sentences.roman: ithe sagḷaṃ mahāg āhe, bādzārāt svasta āhe.
sentences.en: Everything's expensive here; it's cheap at the market.
How much does it come to altogether?

tip.title: Haggling, nicely
tip.body:
- Bargaining is normal at markets and stalls, not in shops with fixed prices.
- Start with **खूप महाग आहे!**, then **जरा कमी करा ना** 'bring it down a bit'.
- **शेवटचं किती?** asks for the final price. **ना** at the end keeps it friendly.

sentences.en: This shopkeeper sells at very high prices.

sentences.native: मला हा शर्ट विकत घ्यायचा आहे.
sentences.roman: malā hā sharṭ vikat ghyāytsā āhe.
sentences.en: I want to buy this shirt.
Could you show me another colour?
This size is too small for me.

sentences.native: मला ही चप्पल बदलून हवी आहे.
sentences.roman: malā hī tsappal badlūn havī āhe.
sentences.en: I'd like to exchange these sandals.
I don't want such big trousers.
I don't have that much money on me.

sentences.native: हीच साडी लाल रंगात आहे का?
sentences.roman: hīts sāḍī lāl raṅgāt āhe kā?
sentences.en: Do you have this same sari in red?
I need to exchange these sandals.

sentences.native: एवढा मोठा साईझ नको, जरा लहान दाखवा.
sentences.roman: evḍhā moṭhā sāīz nako, dzarā lahān dākhvā.
sentences.en: Not such a big size, show me a smaller one.

tip.title: Paying: द्या, घ्या, चालेल का?
tip.body:
- **द्या** 'give' and **घ्या** 'take' are the polite forms of देणे and घेणे; to a friend: **दे**, **घे**.
- **… चालेल का?** asks whether something is OK: कार्ड चालेल का?
- No change? **सुटे पैसे नाहीत.**

sentences.en: Do you have change for five hundred?
Give me a hundred rupees back, please.
Give me the receipt, will you? (informal)
